lines: Eight low-frequency oscillators in one panel, each with its own shape, rate, pulse width and phase, and all of them able to run as divisions of a tempo voltage from vcClk
Blends the wave of that oscillator across the knob's travel, from sine through triangle and sawtooth to square
Multiplies the shape knob by a tenth of this voltage, so 10V gives the shape the knob is set to and a patched cable at 0V forces a sine whatever the knob says
Sets that oscillator's frequency as a power of two in hertz, the exponent running from -8 to 13; a tempo at the sync input replaces that with a division of the tempo
Adds to the rate knob, 10V adding 21 to the exponent, and the total is held between -8 and 13; with a tempo at the sync input 10V moves the division by 8 steps instead
Sets the width of the square wave in that row as a fraction of the cycle, held between 0.01 and 0.99, and it changes nothing until the shape knob has brought the square into the blend
Multiplies the pulse width knob by this voltage plus 1 and then by 0.05, so a patched cable at 0V leaves a twentieth of the knob setting and it takes 19V to get the knob back
Offsets where that oscillator starts in its cycle, a whole cycle across the knob's travel, the centre giving half a cycle
Adds to the phase knob, 10V shifting a whole cycle, and the total is held to one cycle
Sends every oscillator back to the start of its cycle when pressed
Sends every oscillator back to the start of its cycle on a rising edge; any voltage away from zero counts as high, negative ones included
Adds 5V to all eight outputs, moving them from ±5V to 0-10V
With a tempo at the sync input, changes the rate knobs from a list of fixed divisions to a continuous rate that is the cube of the knob; with the sync input empty it changes nothing
Sets the tempo the rate knobs divide, 1V for every 60 bpm, where the maker's manual says 1V for every 50 bpm
Holds every oscillator where it is in its cycle while it is held down
Holds every oscillator where it is in its cycle while the voltage here is away from zero, negative ones included
The wave from that row, ±5V unless the offset switch has been flipped
Note — an oscillator runs only while its own output jack is patched; with that cable out the row is held at 0V and its phase does not advance
Note — with the sync input empty the rate knobs read as frequencies; patch a tempo there and they step through 17 fixed divisions of it, the centre of the knob giving one cycle every four beats

CatroModulo_CM-1.notes: Read at commit d55cb70, the head of the repository; 80422ac is the commit that set plugin.json to the installed 2.0.0 and the only change after it is bf6f969, a round to roundf in CM-9 that the merge d55cb70 brought in. The maker's manual, CM-manual-v0.6.5.pdf in the repository, states the bpm voltage standard as 1V per 50 bpm; CM_BpmClock::cvtobpm at CatroModulo.hpp:642 multiplies by 60, so a volt is 60 bpm, and every module in the plugin uses that function. The pulse width input is scaled knob*(1+V)*0.05, which is almost certainly a slip for knob*(1+V*0.05) or similar: a patched cable at 0V cuts the pulse width to a twentieth of the knob and unity needs 19V. The shape, rate, pulse width and phase inputs all replace rather than add to their knobs when a cable is present, and the shape, pulse width and select-style inputs multiply the knob, so a patched cable at 0V zeroes the control. Nothing in this plugin is polyphonic: the source has no setChannels, getPolyVoltage or getChannels anywhere. The plugin adds no context menu items of any kind.

CatroModulo_CM-2.notes: Read at commit d55cb70. With a row's signal input empty but its output patched, line 74 puts out the attenuverter knob multiplied by the offset knob, which makes the row a constant voltage source rather than a silent one. The mix output divides by the number of rows whose input jacks are patched, not by eight, and the x2 switch multiplies after the ±10V clamp, so both the row outputs and the mix can leave the module at ±20V.

lines: Eight dials whose values can be stored in eight slots and played back, either by choosing a slot by hand or by stepping through the slots in one of sixteen patterns
Sets the direct value for that output between -1 and +1, and with a cable in its input attenuates that voltage instead
Multiplies that dial by a tenth of this voltage, so 10V gives the dial's own setting and a patched cable at 0V holds that direct value at zero
The direct value of that dial crossed with the stored one by the morph slider, scaled to ±10V
Stores all eight direct values into that slot when pressed, replacing what was there
Stores all eight direct values into that slot on a rising edge; any voltage away from zero counts as high
Crosses each output between its direct dial value and its stored one: centre gives the direct value, the clockwise end the stored value, the counter-clockwise end the two multiplied
Adds to the morph slider, 10V moving it a full step from direct to stored
Chooses which of the eight stored slots feeds the outputs, and with the scan switch on it blends between neighbouring slots instead of snapping to one; it is read only while the sequencer is off
Multiplies the select knob by a tenth of this voltage, so 10V gives the knob's own slot and a patched cable at 0V forces the first slot
Blends between neighbouring slots as the select knob is turned instead of snapping to one; it changes nothing while the sequencer is running
Turns the step sequencer on and off; with it off the select knob chooses the slot and the pattern display reads OFF
Chooses one of sixteen step orders for the sequencer, named on the pattern display, the sixteenth of them picking a slot at random on every step
Multiplies the pattern knob by a tenth of this voltage, so 10V gives the knob's own pattern and a patched cable at 0V forces the first one
Sets how many steps the sequencer runs before returning to the first, 1 to 16, shown on the length display
Multiplies the length knob by a tenth of this voltage, so 10V gives the knob's own length and a patched cable at 0V forces a length of one
Advances the sequencer one step when pressed
Advances the sequencer one step on a rising edge; any voltage away from zero counts as high, and this jack is ignored while a tempo is patched to the bpm input
Runs the sequencer from a tempo instead of the step jack, one step per beat, 1V for every 60 bpm, where the maker's manual says 1V for every 50 bpm
Sends the sequencer back to its first step and restarts the internal clock when pressed
Sends the sequencer back to its first step and restarts the internal clock on a rising edge; any voltage away from zero counts as high
Fills all eight slots with fresh random values when pressed, losing whatever was stored; the dials themselves are left where they are
Fills all eight slots with fresh random values on a rising edge, losing whatever was stored
Note — the eight slots start empty and the eight dials start at zero, so every output reads 0V until a dial is turned; a slot is filled only by its record button or a trigger at its jack
Note — two of the sixteen patterns put a rest between steps, and on a rest all eight outputs drop to 0V

Note — the small white dot beside each dial shows the value coming out of the chosen slot and the yellow ring shows which slot that is; both are drawn by the module and neither can be clicked for help

CatroModulo_CM-3.notes: Read at commit d55cb70. The enum carries a PARAM_Q that is never given a configParam and whose createParam call is commented out at line 316, so it has no widget, no tooltip and no position, and it is left untagged. The sequencer steps from the internal clock whenever the bpm jack is patched, and the step jack and step button are then ignored. Patterns 2 and 3 of the sixteen hold -1 in every other slot, which mutes all eight outputs for that step. The maker's manual gives the bpm standard as 1V per 50 bpm; the code's CM_BpmClock::cvtobpm multiplies by 60. Nothing here is polyphonic.

lines: A tempo clock with a numeric display, three square-wave outputs at half, one and twice the beat, and gold-ringed jacks carrying the tempo itself as a voltage for the other Catro/Modulo modules
Sets the tempo, 0 to 500 bpm, read out on the display
Sets the step the tempo knob moves in across its three positions: 0.01, 1 or 5 bpm
Measures the tempo of a clock patched here and adds it to the tempo knob; it locks on after two pulses of equal spacing and holds that tempo until the spacing changes
Adds to the tempo, 1V for every 60 bpm, where the maker's manual says 1V for every 50 bpm; every output except the plain tempo voltage follows the sum
Restarts the internal clock on a rising edge and drives the reset output to 10V while the voltage here is away from zero
Restarts the internal clock when pressed and drives the reset output to 10V while it is held down
10V while the reset button is held down or the reset input is away from zero, for restarting the other modules at the same moment
The tempo as a voltage, 1V for every 60 bpm, taken before the + input is added
The tempo with the + input added, as a voltage, 1V for every 60 bpm
Half the tempo as a voltage, 1V for every 60 bpm
Twice the tempo as a voltage, 1V for every 60 bpm
A 0-10V square wave at one pulse per beat, half of each cycle high
A 0-10V square wave at one pulse every two beats, half of each cycle high
A 0-10V square wave at two pulses per beat, half of each cycle high
Note — the tempo knob comes up at 0 bpm, so the module makes no pulses at all until it is turned up or a clock is patched to the ext input
Note — the gold-ringed jacks throughout Catro/Modulo carry a tempo as a voltage rather than as pulses; chain one module's tempo output into the next module's tempo input to hold them all at one tempo

The maker's manual gives the bpm standard as 1V per 50 bpm; CM_BpmClock::cvtobpm at CatroModulo.hpp:642 multiplies by 60 and bpmtocv divides by 60, so a volt is 60 bpm. The plain tempo output at line 79 is written before the + input is added at line 82, so that jack alone ignores the + input while the /2 and x2 tempo outputs and all three pulse outputs follow it. CM_BpmClock::setbpm clamps the tempo it keeps at zero but computes the voltage it reports from the unclamped figure, so a negative voltage at the + input large enough to take the sum below zero stops the clock while the + tempo output reads negative. The ext detector needs two consecutive intervals within 1ms of each other before it locks.

CatroModulo_CM-8.notes: Read at commit d55cb70. Twelve LightIds are configured in the enum and not one of them is ever written in process, and no LightWidget is added for any of them, so they can be neither seen nor clicked. Binary mode rounds the two signals before the four comparison outputs and the clip and fold outputs, but the six threshold gates read the unrounded signals, so binary mode changes half the panel and not the other half. cm_fold in CM_helpers.cpp gives up after fifty reflections and clamps what is left, and returns the lower threshold outright when the two thresholds are equal. Nothing here is polyphonic.

CatroModulo_CM-9.notes: Read at commit d55cb70. The operating mode is a CM_OP widget at CatroModulo.hpp:906, a plain Button rather than a ParamWidget: it is saved in the patch, it changes what every output does, and because it has no ParamQuantity it can never be clicked for help. Whether the module routes one signal to eight or eight to one is decided by which jacks are patched rather than by any control: with no row inputs and no single input it makes gates instead. The reset jack is read only inside the branch that requires the clk jack to be patched, so a reset with no clock does nothing. Eight row inputs, eight row outputs and the single input and output carry whatever is patched through them, so none of them is given a family. Nothing here is polyphonic.

The step pass-through output is not a copy of the step pulse's shape: line 76 reports 10V for any non-zero reading at the step jack, including negative ones, so a bipolar clock comes out of it as a continuous 10V.
